chapter: Quality Serenaders, Cotton Club and union recollections
title: Getting Lionel Hampton out of jail and sobered for the job
summary: Howard tells how he bailed Lionel out of the Long Beach jail and bathed him in time for the Sunday matinee.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: (Laughter)
Something like what?
Playing.
But it sounds like he was sort of a character at that time. Were there a few little problems as a young man?
Yeah, he --
Did you ever have to get him out of trouble or something?
Yeah. Oh, I don't know. You did?
Well, nothing serious, but I mean -- they always have somebody that (inaudible) -- was he late on jobs and things?
I had to get him out of jail. They took him down there -- he went down to Long Beach and got into trouble with some woman, and he was there in jail.
So you were not only a leader. You had to be like, what would you say, father, nursemaid or whatever, to take care of --
I was a nursemaid and a father and everything to Lionel. Not only that, he was a cat that (Inaudible).
It says here that you had to get him out of jail and found him drunk and you had to take him home and
give him a bath and get him sober in time to play the job?
Yeah, took him home and gave him a bath in time to play the job. Doggone it, I forgot all about that.
A band leader really has some responsibilities.
Sunday afternoon. Sunday afternoon, I'll never forget it as long as I live. I had to take him home and give him a bath and then take him back to play.
Would you raise your microphone a little bit?
Yeah. Take him back to play and get him sober.
And he'd probably been going since Saturday night, right?
Yeah, he'd been going all day. Oh, boy.
And --
That was something else. Please excuse me.
